business_problem: Based in Estonia, Wildix has offered unified communications solutions since 2005 and provides services to 2 million users worldwide. The company focuses on enhancing its customers' sales processes through its communications solutions.
solution_summary: With more customers shopping online, and with the rise of remote work, in-store foot traffic isn't what it used to be. Wildix, a provider of unified communications solutions, saw an opportunity to offer innovative support to brick-and-mortar retailers to help them meet these modern challenges. Wildix recognized that to compete with online competitors, in-person stores must be able to offer efficient and personalized customer service with lean staff teams. The company sought to build a solution that could offer near real-time communication through the cloud and integrate with existing and future in-store systems. To modernize quickly, the company chose to build its complete retail headset solution, x-hoppers, on Amazon Web Services (AWS).

solution_components.name: Amazon Redshift
solution_components.role: Serves as the analytics warehouse for the customer and agent support workflows.

solution_components.name: AWS Lambda
solution_components.role: Executes serverless processing and workflow glue for the customer and agent support workflows.

solution_components.name: Amazon Polly
solution_components.role: Generates speech output used by the customer and agent support workflows.

solution_components.name: Amazon Transcribe
solution_components.role: Converts voice interactions into text for the customer and agent support workflows.

data_flow: Push-to-talk communication for in-store associates, broadcasts across multiple departments, and external phone calls can all be handled through the headset and associated application. If a customer asks a question that a store employee doesn't know the answer to, the employee can ask AI in natural language, as if they were asking a knowledgeable colleague. "Using AWS significantly accelerated our innovation process," says Hölzl.
business_outcome: Wildix continues to add more features to x-hoppers. In some cases, Wildix has been able to implement new features directly requested by active customers, such as adding a voice imprint functionality to the headsets to authenticate which employee used which headset during a shift.
metrics: Wildix provides unified communications solutions to 2 million customers worldwide.
